verdicts.evidence: Sheet.tsx:96-105 passes one lg list as lg/md/sm/xs/xxs; Sheet.tsx:107-115 handleChange writes every item of the grid's current-breakpoint layout to onMove; ReportsNext.tsx:217-223 stores it in the draft and ruleOff (:165-171) saves it via encodeSheet (useReportsNextData.ts:180-191). Keyboard path rp-arrange.ts:133-137 colsForWidth returns 6/4/2 below 996px and moveCutting/resizeCutting clamp+compact at that count, fromLayout writes all slots. No media query or guard stops arranging on a narrow container (reports-next.css has only reduced-motion). Container width, not viewport, so a desktop with the sidebar open can hit sm. Pointer path inferred from react-grid-layout behaviour, not executed.

Mechanism holds: useUserPreferences.ts:133 placeholderData {}, :197 isLoading false under placeholder; useReportsNextData.ts:242,348 sheetKnown=!isLoading; sheetKnown is read nowhere in non-test code; ReportsNext.tsx:160-163 copies data.sheet (default via decodeSheet(undefined)) and :165-171 saves the draft. Narrower: the window is the first load of the preferences query only (HouseShell, AskPanel, GroundChoiceSync use the same hook so in-app navigation hits a warm cache, staleTime 30s), so it is a cold deep-load race, not every visit. isPlaceholderData (:205) exists and was not used.
verdicts.corrected_claim: On a cold load of /reports, before the preferences request answers, the page renders and fetches the default sheet; Arrange copies the default and Rule it off saves it over the saved layout. Normal in-app navigation has the preferences already cached.

verdicts.evidence: ReportsNext.tsx:165-171 sets ruledOff true synchronously after data.saveSheet; saveSheet (useReportsNextData.ts:324-329) calls fire-and-forget updatePreferences (useUserPreferences.ts:181-184); onError (:162-169) restores previous silently; updatePreferencesAsync (:193) is not used by the page. Failed PATCH: draft already cleared, view falls back to old sheet, stamp already shown.

No expand/fullscreen/zoom control anywhere under pages/reports/next (only aria-expanded on the Show-the-working toggle rp-plot.tsx:203; AskTheBook is a palette dialog, not a chart view). But cells are not fixed: while arranging the reader can resize to the full 12 columns and any height (SHEET_MIN 3x3 is a floor only, rp-sheet.ts:155-156), and .rp-cut scrolls (reports-next.css:65-84). So bound by its cell, yes; bound to a small cell, no.
verdicts.corrected_claim: No chart has an expand or full-screen view; a cutting can only be read at the size its cell was arranged to (resizable up to full width, min 3x3).

verdicts.evidence: rp-format.ts:32-35 money() -> lib/utils.ts:16-33 formatMoney hard-codes '$' and toLocaleString('en-US'); every register uses money() (rp-registers-trade/house/bench). lib/mudavym/format.ts:70-98 fmtMoney(value, currency) exists and is not imported under pages/reports/next. rp-registers-goals.tsx:91-95 currency unit falls through to figure(v,'compact'), no unit mark. format.ts:75-78 itself records Turkish houses.

Both reads are unranged: advanced-analytics.service.ts:213-220 (loadOrders) and analytics.service.ts:206-213 (loadDeliveredOrders), so PostgREST's 1000-row cap would apply with no truncation flag; tech-debt note :22 lists goals purchase_spend as the same class and the guard scans only pos_checks/wine_consumption_log. Errors: both call logQueryFailure (:221, :217) then return [] - server-logged, not silent in the log, but invisible to the reader. Pacing: rp-registers-trade.tsx:338-340 does print 'No delivered purchase order falls in either 30-day window' on an empty read. Uncosted: total_cost||final_price||0 (:681, :220). Narrower: the cap binding needs more than 1000 orders per window per house, never measured; the real, reachable failure is the error-to-[] path.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The two procurement_orders reads have no range or whole-read refusal, so they would cap at 1000 rows without saying so, and any failed read degrades to [] (logged server-side only), which the pacing register words as 'no delivered purchase order'. Whether any house has reached 1000 orders is unmeasured.

verdicts.evidence: advanced-analytics.service.ts:165 date=(created_at).substring(0,10) is the UTC date; :585-594 builds the series from new Date().toISOString() UTC days then E.dayOfWeekProfile; toDaily :239-255 and getCashflow :680 use UTC substrings. The house timezone is available (:192 selects timezone) but unused here. Till is already house-day (analytics.controller.ts:1191, ADR 0296), so only seasonality/cashflow are affected. tech-debt note :27 files C02/F-129 as open.

getCashflow: loadOrders(restaurantId,180) filters created_at >= since (:220) but buckets by delivered_at (:680), so orders created before the window and delivered inside are dropped. toDaily(…,180) emits yesterday back 180 days (:248, today excluded); weekly buckets are daily.slice(i,i+7) from the oldest (:691-692), 180=25*7+5 so the newest bucket holds 5 days, and holtLinear(weekly,…) at :693 takes it as the latest point. Direction (low) follows from a 5-day sum read as a week; magnitude not simulated.

Confirmed: rp-registers-bench.tsx:80 path is /analytics/overview; select reads only cashflow, seasonality, activeGoals (:84-112); getOverview (advanced-analytics.service.ts:824-844) runs eight lenses. Cashflow, seasonality, goals, financial, inventory-science, menu-engineering and insights each also have their own cutting (rp-registers-*.tsx path lines), so duplication is up to seven siblings, five of them heavy. Not confirmed: '~60 page requests' is the tech-debt note's estimate for the five consumption-reading lenses (:34), explicitly unmeasured.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The bench cutting calls /overview (eight lenses, five of which each read a 90-day consumption window whole) to use three fields; the note's roughly 60 page requests is an unmeasured estimate.

verdicts.evidence: Numbers are printed: rp-registers-trade.tsx:585-587 'Backtest error (MAPE)', :589 raw a.model; rp-registers-house.tsx:546-547 'Table-adjusted fit (R2)'. But these are model backtest/fit statistics, labelled as such. ADR 0104's 'confidence never a number' (0104 header and Context) is about invoice/document extraction confidence, not forecast accuracy. Whether it should extend to model-fit figures is a product reading, not a violation the code proves; the raw model identifier is the clearer leak.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The forecast shows MAPE and a raw model name and the waiters register shows R2; these are model-quality numbers, outside ADR 0104's stated scope (document extraction confidence), so 'violates ADR 0104' overstates it.

verdicts.evidence: rp-format.ts:157-162 failureOf takes error.message (axios status line) not response.data; used at useReportsNextData.ts:308. useReportExports.ts:75 defines reasonOf and :225 uses it, so exports do show the gateway sentence. analytics.controller.ts:200-203 (financial) and :1234-1237 (pos-revenue) wrap every error as HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (also :235-237, :259-261, :294-296 per the note's four routes); tech-debt note :16 and :36 record both as owed.

rp-registers-trade.tsx:238-243 cats data is one row per dailySeries entry with a text label; :215 basis says the series is sparse on purpose, so a missing day is absent and line/area (rp-plot.tsx:327-386) join across it on a categorical XAxis. :161 revenue: num(r.revenue) ?? 0 turns a null into 0. The server row may never be null in practice (not checked), so the 0 is a client-side coercion.

rp-registers-trade.tsx:557 seam.projected = seam.value so the last measured category carries both series; rp-plot.tsx:307-325 renders two <Bar> elements (value, projected) in one BarChart, which Recharts groups side by side per category; the seam category draws a solid and a hatched bar, and every category reserves two slots. 'bars' is offered for this register (graphs list :505).

rp-plot.tsx:494,501-502 call format(v as number) when a cell exists though v may be null. Latent only: the sole matrix producer (rp-registers-trade.tsx:228-235) pushes revenue from num()-coerced numbers, never null, and its format is money(), which returns the em dash for null (rp-format.ts:32-35), so even a null would not crash or print NaN.

rp-plot.tsx:216-217 key={l} on the filtered working lines is real, so two identical lines would warn and collide. The lines are distinct per-register sentences (basis arrays), none seen repeating; reachable only if a register emits the same sentence twice.

reports-next.css:65-70 .rp-cut has overflow:hidden. But the tooltips are plain Recharts <Tooltip> (rp-plot.tsx:272, :414) with no portal or allowEscapeViewBox (grep: none), and Recharts 2 (package.json recharts ^2.10.3) keeps the tooltip inside the chart's own box by default, so it is repositioned rather than escaping the cell. A tooltip taller than a very small chart could still be cut. Not rendered.

ReportsNext.tsx:317-335 builds the cuttings array and every <Cutting> element unmemoised each render with inline closures (onGraph, onSwap, onRemove), so each setDraft from a drag-stop re-renders all Cuttings and Recharts children; useReportsNextData.ts:289-315 recomputes the registers map each render (its own comment :313-314 says results is fresh each render). Cost not measured; the map rebuild itself is cheap.

ReportsNext.tsx:170 window.setTimeout(() => setRuledOff(false), 2400) with no clear. True, but harmless on React 18 (no unmount warning, a no-op set), and the one real effect is that two rule-offs within 2.4 s let the first timer hide the second stamp early.

Cutting.tsx:87 options [7,30,90] against analytics.controller.ts:1204-1207 clamping days to 1-365: true, and the file calls it the only period control. 'No register compares one period with another' is too broad: the pacing register compares spendLast30d with spendPrev30d and paceDeltaPct (rp-registers-trade.tsx:313-345, 362-363) and the bench cutting compares this month with last. What is absent is a period-over-period comparison for the till/revenue.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The till window offers only 7, 30 or 90 days though the API takes 1-365, and the till has no previous-period comparison (purchases do, fixed at 30 vs prior 30).
